settings.content: Palette, spacing, radius and motion are NOT theme settings. They live in the design system and resolve through assets/theme.css — exposing them here would let one edit break the whole system. Only copy and the type pairing are editable.

settings.content: The two values the B2B route and the Shopee hand-off depend on. Both are blank today, and both fail visibly rather than silently: with no WhatsApp number the quote form's button is unavailable and says why, and with no Shopee URL the 'Buy on Shopee' link is simply absent instead of landing on a search page.

settings.label: WhatsApp number
settings.info: In international format. The + and any spaces or dashes are stripped before the link is built, so either form works. This is where every quote enquiry goes — there is no inbox behind the form. Supplied by the studio 2026-09-13 and set as the schema default rather than written into config/settings_data.json, which this theme deliberately does not have: a default is a starting value the studio can still change in the theme editor, whereas a committed settings file would silently overwrite their edit on the next push.

settings.label: Shopee shop URL
settings.info: The fallback for products with no custom.shopee_url metafield of their own. A per-product URL always wins, because it lands the shopper on the piece rather than on the shop.

settings.content: Instagram, Shopee and TikTok. These are THEME settings rather than footer settings because the same three links render in three places — the footer, the home page and the About page — and one section's settings cannot be read from another. A link left blank is not rendered anywhere at all, rather than drawn as a dead control. Paste the full address including https://.

THESE ARE type:text, NOT type:url, AND THAT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Shopify's url setting rejected the TikTok address as an invalid default — the @ in /@wear.label does not pass its validator — and the push reported it as an error on this whole file while completing anyway, which is the failure mode CLAUDE.md warns about. The three URLs ship as schema defaults because this theme has no settings_data.json, so a default that cannot be saved is the same as no link at all. text takes any address. Do not 'fix' these back to url.

settings.label: Shopee
settings.info: Shopee is the studio's own till, which is why it is here at all — Shopify's built-in social settings have no field for it.

settings.label: Handle
settings.info: Shown under each platform name on the home and About page panels. One field because the studio uses the same handle on all three; leave it blank and the panels show the platform name alone.

settings.content: What the Fabric & care section on a product page says. It is keyed by the product's custom.material value, so seventeen products share eight fabrics and eight paragraphs cover the catalogue — the same argument the size chart below is store-wide for. A product with its own custom.care metafield still wins over this.

settings.label: Fabric glossary
settings.info: One fabric per line: material | what it is | how to care for it. The material must match the product's custom.material value exactly, apart from capitals. A material with no line here renders the labelled placeholder rather than another fabric's copy.
settings.default:
linen | Woven from linen, so it breathes in the heat and softens every time you wash it. It creases — that is the fibre doing what linen does, and most of it drops out as you wear the piece. | Hand wash, or machine wash cold on a gentle cycle. Dry in the shade and press on a medium iron while the fabric is still slightly damp.
semiwool | A matte suiting fabric with a clean, heavy drape. It holds the line of a trouser without ever feeling stiff. | Hand wash cold or dry clean. Dry flat in the shade, and press on a low iron with a cloth between the iron and the fabric.
light weight semiwool | The same matte suiting handle as our semiwool, woven lighter. It moves more and sits cooler, which is what makes it the one to reach for in the heat. | Hand wash cold or dry clean. Dry flat in the shade, and press on a low iron with a cloth between the iron and the fabric.
semiwool stripe | Semiwool with the stripe woven into the cloth rather than printed onto it, so the line runs right through and will not lift or fade in the wash. | Hand wash cold or dry clean. Dry flat in the shade, and press on a low iron with a cloth between the iron and the fabric.
crepe stretch | A fine-textured crepe with a little give in every direction. It skims rather than clings, and comes back to shape after a full day of sitting and moving. | Hand wash cold, or machine wash on a gentle cycle. Do not wring. Dry in the shade and press on a low iron if it needs it.
woven twill | A firm diagonal weave with real body to it. It gives a wide leg the weight to fall straight instead of billowing, and it wears in rather than out. | Machine wash cold on a gentle cycle. Dry in the shade and press on a medium iron.
knit | Knitted rather than woven, so it stretches with you and layers without bulk. It relaxes as you wear it and comes back in the wash. | Hand wash cold and never wring. Dry flat in the shade — hanging a wet knit pulls it out of shape — and steam rather than iron.
torino premium | A premium suiting cloth with a smooth face and a quiet sheen. It falls heavily and keeps a clean line from the waist to the hem. | Hand wash cold or dry clean. Dry flat in the shade, and press on a low iron with a cloth between the iron and the fabric.

settings.content: The size chart shown on every product page. It is store-wide on purpose: Wear Label has one size system, and a per-product chart would be the same table typed eleven times and eleven places to correct when one number is wrong. A product that genuinely needs its own chart can still carry a custom.size_chart metafield, and that wins over this.

settings.label: Column headings
settings.info: Comma separated. The FIRST one names the size column. These are trouser measurements because almost everything in the catalogue is trousers — change them if that changes.

settings.label: Rows
settings.info: One size per line, values separated by | and in the same order as the headings above. For example: XS | 64 | 90 | 28 | 72 | 26. Type CENTIMETRES only — the inch column is calculated. Leave this blank and the chart renders a labelled placeholder at its final size rather than a wrong table.

settings.label: Note under the chart
settings.info: Optional. How the garment was measured, for example laid flat. It is what stops a shopper reading a flat measurement as a body measurement.

settings.content: A SECOND chart, for the cardigans and the vest. It is a separate set of fields rather than more rows on the chart above because a top and a trouser are not measured against the same columns — a shopper buying a cardigan measures a chest, not a thigh, and putting both in one table would leave half of every row empty.

THE ROWS ARE PIECES, NOT SIZES, and that is the one thing to understand before editing this. Every top in this catalogue is ONE SIZE — none of the four carries a Size option in Shopify, only Colour — so there are no size rows to build. What varies is the garment: the studio's own figures put Darla Vest at a 110 chest and Nori at 94-100. The studio suggested averaging the three into a single row; that was not done, because the average is 6-7cm off at the chest for two of the three, which on a top is a whole size, and fit is the decision this catalogue is bought on. A row per piece states three true things instead of one false one.

settings.label: Column headings (tops)
settings.info: Comma separated. The FIRST one names the row-header column, which for this chart is the garment rather than a size. The studio's own headings were Panjang Atasan / Lingkar Dada / Panjang Lengan Baju; the site is English, so they are translated here.

settings.label: Rows (tops)
settings.info: ONE GARMENT PER LINE, values separated by | in the same order as the headings above. Type CENTIMETRES only — the inch column is calculated, and a range like 94-100 converts correctly. A dash means the measurement does not apply (a vest has no sleeve) or has not been supplied; both are honest and neither is guessed at. MIU CARDIGAN HAS NO FIGURES — the studio sent three of the four tops. Ask for Miu and fill its row in.
